subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced legacy `MEDIA:` directives stay non-extracting with a delivery-boundary warning, be extracted as attachments, or remain only a documented by-design constraint?
rationale: The current parser intentionally preserves fenced examples as text, but the report describes a real silent attachment-delivery failure; extraction versus diagnostics changes false-positive and user-feedback behavior.

options.title: Warn At Delivery Boundary
options.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one warning only when outbound delivery would otherwise skip the media, and finish review of the linked PR.

options.title: Extract Standalone Fenced Tokens
options.body: Treat standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines as attachments, accepting that code examples could become deliverable media unless stricter policy is added.

options.title: Docs And Prompt Only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on docs plus prompt wording that legacy `MEDIA:` lines must be standalone plain text.

recommendation.title: Warn At Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one warning only when outbound delivery would otherwise skip the media, and finish review of the linked PR.
